changes: Fix [#607](https://github.com/repeat98/modwerk/issues/607): Tape Echo no longer turns the track down. MIX was a linear dry/wet crossfade, so at the default MIX 90 the dry signal was at 29% (-10.7 dB) and a broadband test signal came out 7 to 8 dB quieter. The dry signal now stays at full level through MIX 95 and fades out only above it; the same signal stays within 0.5 dB of its input from MIX 0 to 95 (FDBK 0 and 64, AGE 64). MIX 0 is still exact dry and 127 is still full wet.

Unchanged on purpose: echo level, feedback law, tone and self-oscillation headroom. Raising the echo level to match the input was tried and rejected, because the highest feedback settings then clip the output at full wet (25% of samples at FDBK 102, 68% at FDBK 127, against none before).
Saved projects sound different at the same settings: the dry signal is up to 10.7 dB louder at MIX 90 and the echoes sit lower against it. Lower MIX or the track volume to taste.

Stereo, asked for in the same report, is not planned: a tape echo has one tape and one playback head, so the echo stays mono (the dry signal stays stereo), and a second channel would double its per-track CPU cost while the freeze at seven instances is still open.

Verification is software only: the changed mixer kernel matches the native arithmetic bit for bit on the ColdFire emulator (1,024 blocks across dry, full wet, mixed and ramping MIX), the host voicing gate gained dry-level checks, the browser builder matches native octabam on all 126 Tape Echo selections (54 images, 72 refusals, 0 mismatches) and on the 162 Analog BD compositions, and the USB package was rebuilt (host tests only, no run on a real base). No hardware run, chip timing or listening test exists for this version, and the earlier hardware freeze at seven instances remains open.

Documentation/media-only: retain the exact 0.1.2-experimental runtime and historical UI, source and test evidence while adding a 7.85-second Legowelt Juno 106 chord-pluck preview: dry, clean eighth-note repeats and worn dotted-eighth echoes at 128 BPM, without added gaps. Include pack permission, source/excerpt hashes and offline render settings; refresh monochrome exports from the existing LCD captures.
Retain the approved 0.1.2-experimental runtime and evidence. No DSP behavior, hardware freeze mitigation, timing headroom or new physical-hardware qualification is claimed.

USB package (14 Oct 2026; distribution only, the module source and version are unchanged): loads over USB on a Modwerk base. Its compiled bytes that coincide with stock are rebuilt at install from the reviewed spans of your own OS, which the base checks against its running stock, so the package carries no stock bytes. Emulator and host tests only; no hardware run of this package. The owner waived hardware evidence for this exact version's USB package for the beta.
Documentation-only: add real emulator screenshots of the selection and control pages, access instructions and capture provenance. The firmware implementation is unchanged.
Documentation-only: update author credits in the manifest and guides. The firmware implementation is unchanged.
First Modwerk catalog release of the CPU-based mono tape echo in FX2, with stereo dry output, tape saturation, age and feedback behaviour.
